lastText: File ClosedLogistics Did the RestMinor VictoryAllied Combined Chiefs, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign's human cost lands close to the historical one on the Western front: lighter, by a wide margin, than the war the Soviet Union fought over the same years. Stalin was pressed hard on Poland's postwar government at Yalta rather than accepted on ambiguous terms: a harder line taken exactly where the historical conference chose accommodation. The stand in the Peloponnese broke and the beaches were lost, and what the Germans took in Greece was a division or more instead of the real 14,000. The Mediterranean Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost anyway. Germany's defeat was never a variable Western Allied command decisions controlled, only its timing, its cost, and the shape of the peace that followed it.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
